subject: Clarifying 'no-training' assurances and deletion scenarios — playbook request
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@clearwave.io>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@clearwave.io
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs: 'We do not train on your data' — backups & retention edge cases

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the product demo earlier — Clearwave's legal and infosec teams asked a couple of follow-ups on the training guarantee that I wasn't able to answer on the spot. They want explicit language we can include in our vendor risk review. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm that customer request/ingest data is never used to train models or fine-tune any internal models (no derivatives)?
- What happens to older backups, snapshots, and debugging logs — are those ever retained in a way that could be used for training?
- If we request deletion, what is the timeline and does it cover backups and any cross-region replicas?

If you have a short playbook or matrix we can share with our compliance team, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Emily

--
Emily Stone
Head of Security Programs, Clearwave
security.team@clearwave.io
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@clearwave.io>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: 'We do not train on your data' — backups & retention edge cases

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then I attach a concise playbook and a retention matrix for your review.

1) No-training commitment: Redwood does not use customer request data to train or fine-tune our public models. We offer a non-training pledge for accounts that opt into our private/enterprise controls; that pledge covers both hosted and dedicated modes when the customer selects the "No Model Learning" setting.

2) Backups & snapshots: By default, automated snapshots used for service continuity may be retained for short operational windows (configurable). For customers who select the non-training pledge, we segregate those snapshots and ensure they are excluded from any offline datasets used for model training.

3) Deletion timelines: We support a deletion request workflow. Primary data and live KV caches are deleted within 7 days after a validated request. Snapshots and backups follow a tombstone process and are purged within 90 days by default for non-training pledge customers; for stricter SLAs we can shorten this window contractually and document cross-region replica deletion.

I've attached: redwood-nontrain-playbook-v1.pdf and retention-matrix-2026.xlsx. Mina and Rishi are cc'd to confirm operational details. Happy to jump on a call with your compliance team.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: 'We do not train on your data' — backups & retention edge cases

Emily — adding a few technical clarifications from ops:

- "No Model Learning" flag: triggers isolation in storage and runtime paths. For accounts with the flag, we tag inbound payloads and ensure they never enter our model training pipelines; the tag is enforced at ingestion and in the data lake retention policies.

- Backups & snapshots: operational snapshots are created as EBS-style snapshots and stored in a restricted bucket. For non-training accounts we mark those buckets with a legal-hold-exclusion flag for training pipelines. Backups remain accessible for restore only; we do not materialize them into training corpora.

- Deletion request flow:
  * Step 1 — Validate requester and scope (48 hours)
  * Step 2 — Purge live data and KV caches (within 7 days)
  * Step 3 — Mark snapshots for expedited purge (initiate within 14 days)
  * Step 4 — Confirm cross-region replica removal (complete within 30–90 days depending on replication topology)

We can offer a contractual 30-day purge for snapshots and replicas if Clearwave needs that.

-Mina
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail our GRC team needs. Two follow-ups before we mark the vendor review green:

1) Can you confirm whether debug traces and ephemeral syscall logs are ever routed to any centralized logging cluster used for model research? We have a specific worry about accidental inclusion.
2) For the contractual 30-day snapshot purge, do you have any standard audit evidence (s3 deletion logs, attestations) we can reference during procurement?

If you can provide a short statement I can include in our vendor questionnaire, that'd be helpful.

Best,
Emily
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@clearwave.io>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: 'We do not train on your data' — backups & retention edge cases

Emily — quick, contract-ready statements below you can paste into the questionnaire. If you need a letter on company letterhead we can route this through legal (HS-34291).

1) Training assurance statement: "Redwood Inference does not use Clearwave customer request data to train, fine-tune, or evaluate any of Redwood's public or internal models. For customers who opt into Redwood's 'No Model Learning' setting, all inbound payloads, snapshots, and diagnostic artifacts are excluded from any datasets used for model training."

2) Debug/trace logs: "Debug traces, ephemeral syscall logs, and runtime telemetry are collected for operational diagnostics only. For accounts with the 'No Model Learning' setting, such telemetry is routed to isolated logging clusters and is not included in research or model datasets. Accidental inclusion controls (ingest tags, pipeline rejects, and daily validation checks) are in place to prevent leakage."

3) Snapshot and replica deletion evidence: "Redwood can provide deletion proofs (S3 lifecycle transitions, object-version deletions, and retention tombstone records) as part of contractual obligations. For expedited 30-day snapshot purges, Redwood will provide an audit package including deletion logs and a signed attestation within 45 days of request completion."

Let me know if you want this in a single-page attestation PDF — we can produce one signed by Legal.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Reliability & Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference
